adjectives-adverbs.summary: Degrees of comparison and adjective-adverb confusion.

conjunctions.summary: Linking words and the pairs that go together.

active-passive.summary: Turning a sentence between active and passive.

direct-indirect.summary: Reporting speech: tense, pronoun and time changes.

reading-comprehension.summary: Answering from the passage, not from outside knowledge.

cloze-test.summary: Filling blanks in a passage using grammar and context.

para-jumbles.label: Sentence & para jumbles
para-jumbles.summary: Ordering sentences into a coherent paragraph.

homonyms.label: Homonyms
homonyms.summary: Same word, different meaning: pick the sentence where the word changes sense.

contextual-vocabulary.summary: Pick the word that fits the sentence: tone, collocation and the sense of the blank.

sentence-structure.summary: Parallelism, word order in embedded questions and balanced constructions.

conditionals.label: Conditional sentences
conditionals.summary: If-clauses of all four types, plus unless, wish and as if: which tense goes in which half.

question-tags.label: Question tags
question-tags.summary: The short question added to a statement: the auxiliary, the pronoun and the reversed polarity.

gerund-infinitive.label: Gerund & infinitive
gerund-infinitive.summary: Which verbs and prepositions take -ing, which take to + verb, and the few that take either with a change of sense.

nouns.label: Nouns
nouns.summary: Countable and uncountable, singular-looking plurals, possessives and nouns that take no article or no plural.

confusables.label: Words often confused
confusables.summary: Pairs that are mixed up in the exam: affect/effect, principal/principle, lie/lay, beside/besides.

q-ap-passive.label: Active to passive
q-ap-passive.summary: The object becomes the subject; the verb becomes a form of be + past participle in the same tense; the old subject follows 'by'.

q-ap-active.label: Passive to active
q-ap-active.summary: Undo the passive: the 'by' agent becomes the subject and the verb returns to its active form in the same tense.

q-ap-imperative.label: Passive of a command, request or piece of advice
q-ap-imperative.summary: A command with an object becomes 'Let + object + be + V3'; a command with no object becomes 'You are ordered/requested to + V1'; a piece of moral advice becomes 'Object + should + be + V3'.

q-ap-haveto.label: Passive of 'have/has/had to'
q-ap-haveto.summary: 'Subject + have/has/had + to + V1 + object' becomes 'Object + have/has/had + to + be + V3 + by + subject' — the 'to' stays, and only the verb after it turns into be + past participle.

q-ap-causative.label: Let/bid/help/make take 'to' only in the passive
q-ap-causative.summary: Let, bid, help and make are followed by a bare infinitive in the active voice but by 'to + V1' once the sentence is turned passive.

q-aa-comparison.label: Comparison with 'than'
q-aa-comparison.summary: Choose more or less by the contrast in the sentence; 'more than' can also mean 'beyond'.

q-aa-degree.label: Barely, hardly, merely, scarcely
q-aa-degree.summary: Barely, hardly and scarcely mean 'only just'; merely means 'only'. Choose by sense.

q-ar-ain.label: a or an
q-ar-ain.summary: The choice follows the sound the next word starts with, not its spelling.

q-ar-the.label: When 'the' is needed
q-ar-the.summary: Superlatives, one-of-a-kind things, rivers, ranges, oceans and ordinals take 'the'.

q-ar-none.label: Where no article belongs
q-ar-none.summary: Abstract and uncountable nouns in general, meals, languages, and most proper nouns take none.

q-cz-grammar.label: A blank the grammar decides
q-cz-grammar.summary: A preposition, article, conjunction or verb form that the sentence around it forces.

q-cz-sense.label: A blank the meaning decides
q-cz-sense.summary: Four possible words; the sense of the paragraph picks one.

q-cd-type.label: The tense pair in an if-sentence
q-cd-type.summary: Each kind of condition fixes both halves: real, likely, unlikely or impossible.

q-cd-wish.label: Wish, as if, if only
q-cd-wish.summary: These take the past form for the present and 'were' for every subject.

q-cd-unless.label: Unless, in case, provided
q-cd-unless.summary: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so a second negative is wrong.

q-cf-fit.label: Choose between the confused words
q-cf-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank, and the pair it is usually confused with among the options.

q-cf-spot.label: The confused word inside a sentence
q-cf-spot.summary: One part of the sentence uses the partner word by mistake.

q-cj-correlative.label: Paired conjunctions
q-cj-correlative.summary: No sooner ... than, neither ... nor, either ... or, hardly ... when, not only ... but also: each pair has fixed partners.

q-cj-relative.label: Relative 'when' after a time noun
q-cj-relative.summary: After a noun of time (Monday, the day), when begins a clause giving more detail.

q-cv-fit.label: Fill the blank with the best word
q-cv-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank; pick the word whose meaning matches the clue words around it.

q-di-statement.label: Statements and back-shift
q-di-statement.summary: A past reporting verb pushes the tense back (am -> was, will -> would) and changes time words (yesterday -> the previous day).

q-di-question.label: Reported questions
q-di-question.summary: A yes/no question becomes if / whether with statement order; no 'did', no question mark.

q-di-command.label: Commands and must
q-di-command.summary: Commands become 'told / ordered ... to'; 'must' stays 'must' in speech.

q-di-exclaim.label: Exclamatory and optative sentences
q-di-exclaim.summary: 'Said' becomes 'exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise' for an exclamation, or 'wished'/'prayed' for a 'May ...' wish; the sentence is rephrased as an ordinary 'that' clause, and 'may' becomes 'might'.

q-di-nochange.label: Forms that never shift
q-di-nochange.summary: 'Used to', 'would rather', 'had better', 'had rather' and 'need not' stay exactly as they are; so does a historical fact, a time clause already in the past, or two simultaneous past actions.

q-gi-verb.label: Which form the verb before it takes
q-gi-verb.summary: Enjoy, avoid, mind take -ing; want, hope, decide take to + verb; a few take either.

q-gi-prep.label: After a preposition or a fixed phrase
q-gi-prep.summary: Every preposition is followed by -ing, including the 'to' of look forward to and be used to.

q-gi-bare.label: Verbs followed by the bare verb
q-gi-bare.summary: Make, let, see, hear and had better take the verb with no 'to'.

q-hm-sense.label: Sentence with a different sense of the word
q-hm-sense.summary: A sentence fixes one meaning of a word; choose the option where the word means something else.

q-idiom-meaning.label: Meaning of an idiom
q-idiom-meaning.summary: An idiom in inverted commas; pick the option that gives its meaning.

q-nn-count.label: Nouns that take no 'a' and no plural
q-nn-count.summary: Information, advice, furniture, luggage, machinery, scenery and poetry have no plural in -s.

q-nn-number.label: Singular-looking plurals and plural-looking singulars
q-nn-number.summary: News, physics and mathematics are singular; scissors, trousers and premises are plural.

q-nn-poss.label: The apostrophe and the of-form
q-nn-poss.summary: People and time take 's; lifeless things usually take 'of'.

q-ows.label: One word for a phrase
q-ows.summary: A phrase is given; pick the single word that means the same.

q-pj-para.label: Arrange sentences into a paragraph
q-pj-para.summary: Four sentences with connectors (However, This, Consequently, In addition): find the opener, then follow the links.

q-pj-process.label: Arrange steps of a process
q-pj-process.summary: Short passive steps (gathered, examined, designed, applied): put them in the order a real process runs.

q-ph-meaning.label: Meaning of a phrasal verb
q-ph-meaning.summary: A phrasal verb in a sentence; pick what it means there.

q-ph-fit.label: The phrasal verb that fits
q-ph-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank; pick the phrasal verb whose meaning the sentence needs.

q-pr-collocation.label: Preposition in a fixed phrase
q-pr-collocation.summary: Many nouns and verbs take a particular preposition: under pressure, under conditions, in danger, on duty.

q-pr-gerund.label: Noun + preposition + -ing
q-pr-gerund.summary: After a noun such as reputation, habit, chance, way, the preposition is followed by -ing, not by to + verb.

q-pr-object.label: Verbs that take the person directly
q-pr-object.summary: Ask, tell, request, advise take the person with no preposition: asked the student to submit.

q-pn-case.label: Subject and object forms
q-pn-case.summary: I, he, she, we, they do the action; me, him, her, us, them receive it or follow a preposition.

q-pn-agree.label: Agreement with the noun it stands for
q-pn-agree.summary: Each, every, everyone, nobody and a singular noun take a singular pronoun.

q-pn-reflexive.label: Myself, himself, themselves
q-pn-reflexive.summary: A reflexive is used only when the doer and the receiver are the same, or for emphasis.

q-pn-relative.label: Relative pronouns
q-pn-relative.summary: Who for people, which for things, that for either, whose for possession, whom as an object.

q-qt-tag.label: Choose the question tag
q-qt-tag.summary: Match the auxiliary and the subject, and turn the polarity the other way.

q-rc-detail.label: A fact the passage states
q-rc-detail.summary: 'According to the passage ...': the answer is a line you can point to.

q-rc-main.label: Main idea or key distinction
q-rc-main.summary: What the passage is mostly about; the idea that most of its sentences support.

q-rc-inference.label: Implied meaning or reason
q-rc-inference.summary: A reason or implication that follows from what is said but is not word for word in the passage.

q-rc-remedy.label: Cause, remedy or deciding factor
q-rc-remedy.summary: What causes a problem, what the author suggests to fix it, or what decides an outcome.

q-ss-parallel.label: Parallel structure
q-ss-parallel.summary: Items joined by 'and', 'or', 'not ... but' must have the same grammatical form.

q-ss-order.label: Word order in embedded questions
q-ss-order.summary: Inside a sentence, a question word is followed by statement order: where he is staying, not where is he staying.

q-spell-correct.label: Pick the correct spelling
q-spell-correct.summary: Four spellings of one word; only one is right.

q-spell-misspelt.label: Find the misspelt word
q-spell-misspelt.summary: Four different words; one of them is spelt wrongly.

q-sva-each.label: Each, every, either, neither
q-sva-each.summary: Each, every, either, neither and words like everyone take a singular verb.

q-sva-nearer.label: Either...or, neither...nor
q-sva-nearer.summary: With either...or and neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

q-sva-number.label: The number of / a number of
q-sva-number.summary: 'The number of' is singular; 'a number of' is plural.

q-sva-phrase.label: Along with, as well as
q-sva-phrase.summary: The verb agrees with the first subject, not with the noun after 'along with' or 'as well as'.

q-sva-spot.label: Subject far from its verb
q-sva-spot.summary: Long sentences put phrases between the subject and the verb, or make a whole clause the subject; find the real subject and check the verb.

q-sva-inverted.label: Verb before its subject
q-sva-inverted.summary: After 'so + adjective', 'here', 'there' and similar openers the verb comes first; it still agrees with the subject that follows.

q-syn.label: Closest in meaning
q-syn.summary: One capitalised word; pick the option closest in meaning.

q-ant.label: Opposite in meaning
q-ant.summary: One capitalised word; pick the option opposite in meaning.

q-tn-modal.label: Verb form after a modal or auxiliary
q-tn-modal.summary: After will, can, may, must, should and similar, the verb is the bare base form, even when other words come in between.

q-tn-subjunctive.label: Verb after demand, insist, suggest
q-tn-subjunctive.summary: After demand, insist, suggest, recommend, request + that, use the base verb, with no -s and no tense.

q-tn-stative.label: Verbs that cannot take -ing
q-tn-stative.summary: Verbs of perception, mental state, feeling and possession (know, believe, want, own, have=possess, resemble, seem) describe a state and never take the continuous form.

q-tn-sincefor.label: 'Since' a point, 'for' a length
q-tn-sincefor.summary: 'Since' names the point a period began (since 2019, since Monday) and pairs with a simple-past clause; 'for' names the period's length (for two years) and never follows 'since'.

q-tn-definite.label: Present perfect with a named past time
q-tn-definite.summary: The moment a sentence names a finished point in time (yesterday, last year, in 2016, two days ago), the verb must be simple past, not present perfect.

q-tn-sequence.label: Past perfect / future perfect for the earlier action
q-tn-sequence.summary: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect (before/after/by the time/found that); when the same signpost points at the future, the later action takes the future perfect.

q-tn-itstime.label: 'It's time' + simple past, not a modal
q-tn-itstime.summary: 'It is (high) time' is followed by a subject and the simple past, or by 'to' and the base verb with no subject — never by a modal such as 'should'.
